svg.title: A client opening a listen stream and an update arriving back down it
svg.desc: A sequence diagram with a client lifeline on the left and a server lifeline on the right. Step one, the client POSTs subscriptions slash listen carrying a notifications filter that sets resourcesListChanged true and names one URI in resourceSubscriptions, with a note that the two omitted fields mean those types are not subscribed to. Step two, the server answers with notifications slash subscriptions slash acknowledged, which must come first and carries the subscription id in the reserved meta key, that id being the JSON-RPC id of the listen request. An accent-coloured line down the right of the server marks the stream staying open. Off to the side, a box shows work on the server changing the resource and calling notify resource updated. Step three, notifications slash resources slash updated travels back down the open stream carrying only the URI. Step four, the client issues an ordinary resources slash read, which is where the new content actually arrives. Margin notes explain that the response is a long-lived event stream rather than a second connection, that the acknowledgment echoes the subset the server agreed to honor, and that progress and log messages never travel on this stream.
